Because it isn’t correcting the typical JS float artifacts, Safari shows 4.029999999999999. src/util/func.js provides number-precision utilities (e.g. determining decimal length, rounding helpers) that NumberPicker relies on. Both files need to be updated so that after adding step to the current value you force a correct toFixed()/rounding pass using the desired precision, eliminating the floating-point residue.
1.bug_scenario: In Safari, clicking the “+” button on a NumberPicker initialized at 4.02 with a step of 0.01 yields an internal sum of 4.029999999999999 instead of 4.03 (due to JavaScript floating-point precision) and the component displays that incorrect value.

This file computes the new value when the user clicks '+' or '-' and applies a toFixed or similar rounding based on the precision prop. Because it currently performs a direct float addition, Safari (and other browsers) expose the usual JS floating-point imprecision. Fixing the bug requires updating the arithmetic and rounding logic in this file to use a decimal-safe addition (e.g. scaling to integers, using a utility for precise decimal math, then applying toFixed) so that 4.02 + 0.01 correctly becomes 4.03 before display.
